locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_negative_mellin_round17.md · One packet: a large sharp inverse with small weakened norm
statement: Fix a prime p, u_*=log p, b=1/p and 0<A<q. The one-sided packet F_T(u_*+v)=b χ(v/W)η(Tv)sin(Tv), W=log^A(T)/T, has squared N_(−q) norm O(b²[W√T+TW/log^q T]) and tends to zero in this norm. On a=1+ε/2 its sharp inverse at u_* equals b exp((a−1/2)u_*) log(TW)/(2π)+O(b), with O(bW) change for U∈[T,T+1]. The target prime contributes −b log p log(TW)/(2π√p) in the folded contour, while all other prime terms tend to zero and the gamma piece is O(N_(−q)).
hypotheses: Fixed prime, strip margin 0<ε<1/4 and fixed 0<A<q. Constants may depend on the stage, including p,q,A,ε. The packet shrinks strictly between the target prime center and the next prime-power center. The contour statement uses a good height in [T,T+1].

statement: For each fixed strip with 0<ε<1/4 one real smooth f, zero near zero and one and O(x^(−3/2)) at infinity, has finite N_(−q) for every fixed q>0. Its samples f(n) at prime powers and f(1/n) for n≥1 vanish. The ordinary symmetric raw zero sum with multiplicity has a subsequence tending to −∞ and a bounded subsequence. The pole and archimedean terms are absolutely finite.
hypotheses: Use one locally finite escaped-prime packet sequence with q_j=1/j and A_j=q_j/2 before choosing each carrier. Stagewise protection controls both finite-height subsequences. The witness satisfies literal (A) and (B). Its critical norm is infinite, and the weakened norms need not be bounded uniformly as q decreases to zero.

statement: The exponent p=0 is the exact boundary for a universal ordinary symmetric height formula in this logarithmic strip scale. Every p≥0 suffices under the original value bounds and local H¹ around x=1 or the literal (A) class with midpoint values. One smooth witness in that class defeats all weights √(1+t²)/log^q(e+|t|), q>0.
hypotheses: Fix 0<ε<1/4 so both sufficiency and the counterexample apply on the stated strip. This is a universal symmetric result for the stated test class. No individual necessity claim, uniform q-bound, or separate half-axis threshold is asserted.

statement: For K≈T^θ, 1/2<θ<2/3 and integer P≈KT, one nonnegative real sequence b(n) on J=[P,2P)∩ℤ has exact mass P. Writing B_(k,u)=Σ_(n≡u mod k)b(n), the all-residue squared error about P/k totals O(PK) over k≤2K and the sum of row maxima is O(K√P). Both bounds hold on the unit rows centered by their induced means. For the full support S of the narrow-band fourth prime polynomial, including repeated factors, |S|=binom(M+3,4)≍K/log⁴K where M is the number of band primes. The coefficients c_k=4!/∏_(p|k)m_p! satisfy 1≤c_k≤24. The h=1 unit-centered real phase projection with weights c_k/k is ≫√(P|S|), exceeding T log⁴T by a divergent factor.
hypotheses: Fix a narrow relative prime band [X,(1+η)X] with K=X⁴ and (1+η)⁴<2 so S lies in [K,2K). All congruence rows arise from the same sequence and whole-row common-divisor marginals agree. The all-residue centering and induced unit means concern an integer interval, with no prime support, simultaneous unit support, P/φ(k) baseline, or Mangoldt pointwise cap.

statement: In the common-sequence countermodel the weights can be nonnegative integers while preserving mass P, the same order of discrepancy bounds and the phase lower bound. Draw P integers from probabilities b(n)/P. The multinomial summed expected variance is O(PK), and the projection variance O(P(|S|/K)²) is negligible against P|S|. Markov and Chebyshev give a realization satisfying both bounds.
hypotheses: Same single interval, full fourth-power support and centering as the real-weight model. Integer values can include repeated draws. This remains an abstract obstruction and does not estimate the genuine prime term or the full smooth C_* sum.
